content.title: About
content.content: Chicken curry is an Indian dish where bite‑size pieces of chicken are simmered in a fragrant sauce made from spices, tomatoes, and either coconut milk or yogurt. The dish balances heat, sweetness, and creaminess, highlighted by the characteristic aroma of turmeric, coriander, cumin and ginger.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: ‘Curry’ is a generic term for many dishes, not a single spice.
Traditional Indian curry often starts with whole spices toasted in oil (the “tadka”).
Turmeric, the key ingredient, gives the sauce its golden hue and has anti‑inflammatory properties.
Regional variations are wide: southern recipes favor coconut milk, while northern versions use cream or yogurt.
Chicken curry gained worldwide popularity through adaptations to local tastes and ingredient availability.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains beneficial spices
items.content: Turmeric, ginger and garlic offer antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Coriander and cumin stimulate bile production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, zinc and magnesium, supporting immunity and nerve function.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to turmeric, cumin or other spices.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared curry often includes added salt; people with hypertension should watch intake.

items.title: Spiciness level
items.content: Very hot versions can irritate the stomach of those with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Chicken safety
items.content: Use fresh chicken and cook it thoroughly to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot chicken curry with basmati rice, naan, or flatbreads. It can be added to vegetable stews, used as a filling for wraps, or enjoyed as a quick bowl with quinoa.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
